answer: Student Affairs manages student clubs, promotes athletic and creative activities, organizes cultural events and orientation, oversees housing, provides counseling, holds student elections, and handles the Work-Study and Financial Aid programs.

answer: Student Affairs works with student clubs, societies, and councils to organize athletic, cultural, social, artistic, and theatrical activities that help students pursue hobbies, make friends, and develop leadership skills.

answer: Student Affairs offers seminars and workshops on coping with social, psychological, and emotional challenges, plus one-to-one counseling for personal issues and anxieties; contact studentaffairs@rhu.edu.lb or ext. 777.

answer: The Student Representative Committee (SRC) ensures students' voices influence decisions; students elect their SRC representatives annually in transparent, democratic elections.

answer: RHU has two dormitories, one for female and one for male students. Each dorm has a social sit-in area, a study room with internet-connected computers and library resources, and broadband Wi-Fi; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777) for housing.

answer: RHU has an indoor sports center and outdoor tennis, football, and basketball courts; specialists organize activities and tournaments, and varsity teams compete locally and internationally. Contact the Athletic Department at ext. 330.

answer: The Ushers program trains student volunteers to help organize university events, open houses, graduation ceremonies, and new-student orientation, guiding students, parents and guests.

source_quote: Free bus shuttles transport students from the dormitory to the highway in Damour.
answer: Free shuttles run from the dormitory to the Damour highway, and shuttle buses carry students to and from campus from several areas in Lebanon several times per day; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777) for the schedule.

answer: Student lounges offer activities such as chess and ping-pong, and each dorm has two common rooms, one for social gatherings and one for studying.

answer: The RHU cafeteria serves traditional and international cuisine at reasonable prices throughout the day and into the evening, with indoor and outdoor seating.

answer: The University Medical Clinic, in Block I next to the bookstore, has a resident nurse providing preliminary healthcare around the clock; ambulance services are also available around the clock.

answer: RHU pledges students the right to, among others: a supportive learning environment; proper academic advising; dignity and respect; a clear course outline at the start of the semester; timely constructive feedback; unbiased assessment; confidentiality of records; expressing opinions and grievances without retribution; and appealing a judgment deemed unfair.

source_quote: know the program study plan and graduation requirements;
answer: Students are responsible for complying with the bylaws and code of conduct, knowing their study plan and graduation requirements, attending all classes and meeting course requirements honorably, respecting deadlines, being respectful and tolerant, expressing grievances civilly, protecting university property, and representing RHU professionally.

source_quote: Refrain from smoking except in designated spaces.
answer: Expected conduct includes not smoking except in designated spaces, keeping the premises clean, using trash and recycling receptacles, protecting facilities, never cheating or claiming credit for others' work, respecting diversity, and following university bylaws.

answer: The Work Study program lets students work up to 8 hours per week to partially support themselves, earning modest income and gaining work experience; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777).
